text.p: Colombia coach Hernan Diaz admitted on Friday that he has a serious shortage of strikers after Faustino Asprilla and Victor Aristizabal were sent off during Wednesday's defeat by Paraguay.
Problems are building rapidly for the Colombians, who at one stage were runaway leaders of the South American World Cup qualifying group but have now dropped to second after two successive defeats.

Asprilla, leading scorer in the competition with six goals, was sent off after clashing with Paraguay goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert in the match in Asuncion which Paraguay won 2-1. Colombia's next game is at home to Peru on April 30.
Aristizabal, who plays for Sao Paulo in Brazil, had already been substituted but was also shown the red card after he became embroiled in a brawl which followed the Asprilla-Chilavert incident.

Gomez is already without the services of Asprilla's regular striking partner Ivan Valenciano, who has undergone a knee operation. Possible new faces include Walter Escobar and Victor Bonillo of Deportivo Cali and Jorge Ramirez of Tolima.

Gomez did not rule out recalling former international strikers Adolfo Valencia, Antony de Avila or even Albeiro Usuriaga who was dropped from the national team squad in 1990. Usuriaga now plays for Independiente.
Gomez and his predecessor Francisco Maturana, now in charge of Ecuador, have been remarkably reluctant to bring in new faces.
Players such as Wilmer Cabrera, Freddy Rincon, Leonel Alvarez and captain Carlos Valderrama have been regular fixtures for the best part of a decade.

Another problem is in goal where Farid Mondragon is under fire. He blundered to allow Argentina to score the only goal of February's clash in Barranquilla and was criticised again for his display on Wednesday.
The Colombian soccer federation said on Friday they would send FIFA, soccer's governing body, a video which they said contained evidence that Chilavert attacked Asprilla off the field.
The federation hope the video, shown on the CMI channel's new programme, will limit the punishment for Asprilla and Aristizabal.
